changes.text: 格兰特回信拒绝会面之后，李再次来信。据格兰特记述，他这一方的两位指挥官米德和谢里登起初都对是否停火非常犹豫，怕这不是真心求和；而且李的北弗吉尼亚军团已无路可逃，除非用诡计脱身。不过他们最终同意停火两小时，以便在这段时间里设法与格兰特联络。可这封信送得很费劲：由于格兰特所走的路线，在这一约定的时限内，信使很可能无法把信送到他手里并带回答复，除非穿过南军战线。因此，李派人护送带信的军官穿过自己的战线，把信送到格兰特手里。

After Grant's refusal, Lee wrote again. Grant records that Meade and Sheridan, two commanders on his own side, both hesitated very considerably about suspending hostilities at all. They were afraid the overture was not in good faith; and Lee's Army of Northern Virginia was where it could not escape except by some deception. They finally consented, however, to a suspension of hostilities for two hours, to give an opportunity of communicating with Grant in that time if possible. But the message was hard to deliver: from the route Grant had taken, it would probably not be possible to reach him and get an answer back within the time fixed unless the messenger passed through the rebel lines. Lee therefore sent an escort with the officer bearing the message through his own lines to Grant.
至于叫停鸣炮，一种解释是，受降条件里最后一项从不写在纸上：那是受降消息传开后胜利方作出的表态。作者提出的替代做法是，把收缴佩刀之类的要求当作威慑保留下来，让对方记住谁说了算。作者推断，代价可能是执行阶段对方不愿配合，因为部分执行环节需要对方配合——比如连队或团级长官要为所部具结，李留下的将领要与负责宣誓遣散的北军将领协商、协助此事。

As for halting the salute, one reading is that the last clause of any surrender is never set on paper: it is the stance the winning side takes once news of the surrender spreads. The alternative the writer offers is to keep demands such as handing over side-arms on the books as a reminder of who is in charge. The writer infers that the cost might be an unwillingness to cooperate in the carrying out, since parts of it needed the other side's cooperation — company or regimental commanders signing paroles for the men of their commands, and the generals Lee left behind conferring with the Union generals in charge of the paroling to help with that work.

1865年4月8日（原文只写“8日”，月份与年份据原文所录次日电报的日期1865年4月9日推定），联邦一方的格兰特随己方的波托马克军跟在李的后面追击；李是南军北弗吉尼亚军团的统帅。格兰特正犯着重头痛，在路边一处离大部队有一段距离的农舍过夜，把脚泡进热水和芥末，手腕和后颈贴上芥末膏，指望天亮就能好。李来信提议会面，但按格兰特的说法，会面的目的并不是交出军队。格兰特的回信很干脆：他无权谈和，这样的会面不可能有好结果；和平的条件众所周知，南方只要放下武器，就能让和平早点到来，救下成千上万条人命和数以亿计尚未被毁的财产。

On April 8th, 1865 (the source says only "the 8th"; the month and year are inferred from the telegraph it reproduces from the following day, dated April 9th, 1865), Grant, on the Union side, followed his Army of the Potomac in pursuit, in rear of Lee, the commander of the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia. Grant was in the grip of a sick headache. He spent the night at a farmhouse on the road, some distance behind the main body of the army, bathing his feet in hot water and mustard and putting mustard plasters on his wrists and the back of his neck, hoping that by morning he would be cured. A letter from Lee proposed a meeting, but, as Grant tells it, for a different purpose from that of surrendering his army. Grant's answer was brisk. He had no authority to treat on the subject of peace, and the proposed meeting could lead to no good. The terms on which peace could be had, he wrote, were well understood: let the South lay down its arms, and the most desirable event would come sooner, sparing thousands of lives and hundreds of millions of property not yet destroyed.

dispositions.rationale: 按原文顺序重排：先写米德、谢里登犹豫，最终同意停火两小时；再写在这一时限内信使按格兰特的路线来不及往返，因此李派人护送信使穿过战线。删去“另据／Separately”，未补入其他细节。

evidence.quote: They, however, finally consented to a suspension of hostilities for two hours
they would probably not be able to communicate with me and get an answer back within the time fixed

dispositions.rationale: 删去“真正要办的事都得靠对方的人去做”这一事实口吻的断言，改为明确标出的作者推断：只有部分执行环节需要对方配合，举出证据所载的连、团长官具结，以及李留下的将领与北军将领协商、协助宣誓遣散。把“当天说的第一句话”改为“受降消息传开后胜利方作出的表态”，保留“一种解释是”。ev 增补 E28。

evidence.quote: General Lee leaving Generals Longstreet, Gordon and Pendleton for them to confer with in order to facilitate this work
each company or regimental commander sign a like parole for the men of their commands
When news of the surrender first reached our lines

dispositions.rationale: 首句补上1865年4月8日，并注明原文只写“8日”，月份和年份是据原文所录次日电报的日期1865年4月9日推定的。中英文同步，没有增加其他事实。

evidence.quote: On the 8th I had followed the Army of the Potomac in rear of Lee
